craft_notes: Sthāyin: the distinction — kalā vs tattva. Sanskrit-first: nirūpyate kept is-delineated; yathā/tathā kept the simile-frame; ekarūpakalanāsahiṣṇutvāt kept the defining ablative whole. Rows: 9 (tattva/kalā pair), 2 (long simile spilling), 1 ('enduring one-form classifications' closes — the defining property last). Close: 'enduring one-form classifications.' Rejected: compressing the double yathā/tathā — killed: the frame is the definition; 'endures classification' — kept whole (sahiṣṇutvāt is endurance-of). Read aloud: THE-ka-LĀ-PATH, SET a-GAINST-it: AS-in-WORLDS, WHAT-goes-a-LONG as-FORM is-TATT-va; SO-in-TAT-tvas, CLASS by-CLASS, WHAT-ev-ER-goes-a-LONG as-FORM is-KA-LĀ — END-ur-ing ONE-form-CLAS-si-fi-CA-tions.

lines: as in worlds, what goes along as form
is tattva; so in tattvas, class by class,
whatever goes along as form is kalā —
l4.sanskrit_cite: kalādyadhvā tu nirūpyate tatra yathā bhuvaneṣu anugāmi kiṃcid rūpaṃ tattvam ity uktam tathā tattveṣu vargaśo yat anugāmi rūpaṃ tat kalā ekarūpakalanāsahiṣṇutvāt

reads_against.argmap: What is the kalā-path, and how does it differ? → Kalā is defined against tattva: same 'goes-along-as-form' pattern, but class-wise and classification-enduring — path distinguished from ground.
c1_essence: The kalā-path is delineated against it: whatever goes along as form class-wise — classification-enduring — is kalā.
